page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6455B processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, a 60 MB L3 cache, and 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores placing in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong performance in the top 25%. Multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally fall within the average range, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 8648.24 and a large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 70.75 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 10.89 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r7iz.2xlarge delivers high-frequency processing combined with a dense DDR5 memory configuration, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that also require high single-threaded CPU performance. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the baseline network bandwidth is limited to 3 Gbps, which may act as a bottleneck for data-intensive transfers.

This configuration is suited for database operations, memory-intensive applications, software compilation, and text processing tasks. It also supports light language model inference, achieving an average of 71.94 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B model.
